quest.title: A Series of Twists and Turns
quest.description: After some time, you decide to return to the Palais Mermonia to check up on your Saurian friend.
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x20, Mora x20000, Hero's Wit x2

chapter.title: A Series of Twists and Turns

talks.objective: Wait until the morning of the day after tomorrow (08:00 – 10:00)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey everyone, we're here!

dialogues.speaker: Cacucu
dialogues.text: Oh, hey, my little dudes! Good morning!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Morning, little dude!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh wow, Cacucu's learned a new greeting!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Is that good news or bad news, though?

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Sorry, I did everything within my power. But so far, I've only managed to teach him how to say "good morning."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, so that's all you've been up to this whole time!?

dialogues.speaker: Cacucu
dialogues.text: Get outta here!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I think that means "no."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, so good mornings aside, please tell Paimon, there's been some other progress too?

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Of course. That's why I'm here.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Cacucu's not the only one that Mr. Wriothesley's been getting to talk. I'm referring, of course, to the convicts.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: It was nothing. These guys weren't exactly tough nuts to crack.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So? What's the deal?

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: After racking their brains, they remembered speaking to an inconspicuous middle-aged man just as they were preparing to pack up and leave Natlan.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: He was dressed in the manner of the Children of Echoes and carrying a box — plus, the description matches the one the gun was found in. All in all, he didn't look any different from your average Natlanese traveler.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Perhaps seeing that they were dressed as merchants, this man stopped for a chat, inquiring where their goods were headed and even asking if they could share a boat.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: The smugglers were very cautious, though. They didn't tell him any specifics.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: But all this happened before I crossed paths with them.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: I happened to notice them as they were preparing to set sail. I thought they looked shady, so I snuck aboard, and ended up being carried along all the way to Fontaine...

talks.objective: Go to the Palais Mermonia to find out what's happening
A few days ago, at Romaritime Harbor

dialogues.speaker: Kanaka
dialogues.text: Boss, do we know if those Fontainians will even like this stuff? What if we can't shift it...?

dialogues.speaker: Banolkax
dialogues.text: ...And that's why we call you a rookie. It's all supply and demand, kid. Supply and demand! Natlan's foreign trade is just starting to lift off... There'll be a market for it, you'll see.

dialogues.speaker: Chajal
dialogues.text: That's right. So stop giving the boss trouble, rookie. Just do your job and keep an eye on the goods.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: (Are they merchants? Have they come to Fontaine to do business?)

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: (Scarred face, callused hands...)

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: (On closer inspection, the fabric looks worn at the knees and elbows, and his fingernails are dirty... Not exactly your typical merchant.)

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: (Could he have previously been a warrior, or even an adventurer?)

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: (Something feels off. I'd better sneak up and get a closer look.)

talks.objective: Approach quietly and find out what the suspicious folk are up to

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: (Looks like I've gathered enough intel about the smugglers and their contraband. Time to inform port security.)

talks.objective: Find a way to create a diversion so you can investigate the cargo
Approach quietly and find out what the suspicious folk are up to
A few days ago, at Romaritime Harbor
Discuss the case with everyone present

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: So bottom line, this was an individual smuggler at work.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Exactly. And it was the location itself that caused the deal to fall through.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: The last thing they would have expected was for a quiet beach to turn into a bustling film convention overnight.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Not only is the area now packed with tourists, but the Spina di Rosula have a presence there... I'll bet that both parties were completely caught off guard.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Great job, Lepine-Pauline!

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: That sounds like a plausible theory, but how do we verify it?

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Looks like your people better start rolling up their sleeves.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: How so?

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Easy. Just follow the usual procedure by putting up a lost-and-found notice.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: The more routine we make it seem, the more likely the suspect will come forward to claim it. Even if they send a proxy, we're liable to get our hands on new leads.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: And timing-wise... It's about time we updated the bulletin board anyway.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: All we need now is a lucky Gestionnaire to write up the notice for us, post-haste.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Ah, so that's what you meant by "rolling up their sleeves"...

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: In that case, I may as well write it myself.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Delegating this to someone else would require an additional explanation...

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Hah, or are you just not used to asking others to work overtime?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is that really a major concern here!?

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Well, looks like I won't be needed around here — at least until the notice has been posted.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: You could always wait here if you like. The Palais Mermonia serves a particularly fine cup of tea, if that swings it for you.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Thanks, but no thanks. I left a very noisy creature with a friend before heading out, so I should probably get back to feed it.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Ah, I wasn't aware that you had a pet, Mr. Kinich.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Speaking of pets...

dialogues.speaker: Cacucu
dialogues.text: Get outta here! Outta here!

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Yep, that's the plan. Outta here, indeed.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: I believe that what Wriothesley is trying to say is, you are free to leave, Mr. Cacucu.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Furthermore, it has been determined that Mr. Cacucu should not, in fact, be classified as a flying object. As such, he shall be free to move around Fontaine whenever he so pleases.

dialogues.speaker: Cacucu
dialogues.text: You're the best, bro!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Oh, that really is good news! {NICKNAME}, should we bring Cacucu back to Ifa and Ororon?

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: I shall leave him in your capable hands.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Indeed.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Ajaw.

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: What? What now?

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Let's shake hands.

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: Fine by me. Get ready for a knuckle sandwich!

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Whoa, nice dodge!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uhh... Paimon feels strangely inclined to keep a safe distance...

dialogues.speaker: Cacucu
dialogues.text: D'you miss me, bro?

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Hahaha, Cacucu, you're free!

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: Ugh, not you again! Nope, didn't miss you in the slightest!

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: #Hey, {M#Gramps}{F#other Granny}.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: And hey, Paimon and Kinich, it's good to see you all. Thanks for bringing Cacucu back.

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: Get it away! Get it away from me!

dialogues.speaker: Cacucu
dialogues.text: Nice to meet you, bro!

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: Who are you calling "bro"!? Say that again, to my face! I dare you!

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: If you've got the energy to argue this much, you're clearly not hungry yet.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Let's go find something to eat, while Ajaw lives his best life.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sounds good to me.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Haha, poor Ajaw! He's spent all day being tormented by Ororon, only to discover that the suffering's just begun.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Ifa, as a Saurian vet, how can you just sit back and watch our little dragon-bro suffer?

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Huh? How am I the bad guy?

dialogues.speaker: Cacucu
dialogues.text: Do you even hear yourself?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Doesn't anyone wanna hear how Cacucu got out of jail?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Amidst the racket, you briefly explain what happened with Cacucu to Ifa and Ororon.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Hearing that Cacucu now has permission to move around freely, Ajaw's face goes even redder than before.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Ahh... Y'know, all this has made me realize that I'd quite like to have a pet.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: If that proves inconvenient within the Fortress of Meropide, perhaps you should consider finding a place in the Court of Fontaine?

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: ...That actually sounds like a good idea.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: In the past, I always dismissed the idea of buying a property in the city. The prophecy about the floods meant it never seemed like a worthwhile investment. But now...

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: This might be a good time for you to re-examine the documents I gave you regarding your title as Duke.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Citizens with honorary titles are eligible for certain benefits when purchasing property in the Court of Fontaine.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Really?

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: How about this: You read through your documents from start to finish, while I write up the lost-and-found notice.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh... Looks like there were quite a few others with the same idea...

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Hello, you two.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Have there been any developments?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Okay, guess not...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, the notice was only just posted. Guess it's pretty unlikely that someone would show up right a—
Special Patrol, open up!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whaaa! Who's there? What's going on!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Th—The Special Patrol...?

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: I don't think that's who this is.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, this isn't the time for silly jokes! Let's go check it out...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: A guard from the Palais Mermonia carefully opens the door, and a familiar figure walks in...

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: Good day, all. Gramps, grannies, aunts and uncles.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What in the Teyvat are you doing here, Ororon?

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: Oh, he must be the one you mentioned... Cacucu's owner?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: One of his owners, kind of...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But... Bro, what are you doing here?

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: I'm here to claim a lost item.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Can't tell if he's being deadpan, or deadly serious...

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Is this... the person you saw on the boat, Mr. Kinich?

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: Somehow, I highly doubt that.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: For starters, he just addressed us as "gramps and grannies." And unless this is the youngest-looking middle-aged man in the world, I don't think he's our guy.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I apologize for my grandson bursting in like this...

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: Huh? Was there... something wrong with my door-knocking etiquette? Hmm, that's how they do it in all the films...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's not door-knocking etiquette... That's the Special Security and Surveillance Patrol doing their job. Completely different things.

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: Oh, I see... I figured it was just a polite way of requesting entry, to show the people inside you had something important to discuss.

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: Oh, sorry about that, I totally goofed that one up. Gimme a moment, I'll go back out and try again...

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: Ahem... So, Ororon, you said you were here to claim a lost item. What did you lose?

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: Yeah, so basically...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Ororon carefully describes the lost item he's come to claim. From the style of the box to the gun itself, everything matches.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: For real, now? C'mon, bro...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Is arresting my dear grandson what it's come to...?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ororon, be honest now — were you the one who lost this?

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: No, it belongs to a friend.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So it belongs to Ifa?

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: Of course not, Ifa has his own gun.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uhh...

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: Alright then... Ugh, I knew this wouldn't go well.

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: So here's what went down... This morning, Ifa and I were playing rock paper scissors. Before long, he'd lost — as he usually does — so we figured we'd head out and visit some of the Court of Fontaine's famous landmarks.

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: When we got near the plaza, a man suddenly stopped us to ask for help.

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: He said that he had lost something, and that someone had found it and sent it over to the Palais Mermonia.

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: But apparently he used to work here, and was worried it'd be awkward bumping into his old coworkers, so he asked us to pretend to be the owners and claim it on his behalf.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You didn't manage to keep that pretense up for long...

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: It's fine. I'm not the one who feels awkward, anyway.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: So, a former employee of the Palais Mermonia? ...Was this individual a Fontaine native?

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: Yes, at least I assumed so. He looked like a well-dressed gentleman to me.

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: We were about to refuse, but he was so polite...

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: Could it have been a disguise?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, oh no... Ororon, Paimon thinks you've been tricked. This person might be in cahoots with the bad guys...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Maybe he already took off and escaped, as soon as your mission went pear-shaped!

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: No way, I'm not that dumb.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh?

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: He's not going anywhere. Ifa and Cacucu are keeping an eye on him over at the plaza.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: "Keeping an eye on him." I like the sound of that...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Nicely done, bro.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: In that case, let's hurry over to where Ifa is!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Time to catch that con man and find out what's really going on here.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: Wait a minute, I have a question first.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, you're pretty famous in Natlan, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We're basically household names! But why do you ask?

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: Ha...

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: Would that... be a problem?

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: Remember when I said that the seller might be watching in secret?

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: If so, then picking Ororon to do their dirty work was a careless mistake on their part.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: It suggests that the person who got Ororon to claim the item might not be fully in the know themselves.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: ...There are plenty of unanswered questions, but standing around racking our brains won't help.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: #However, I still suggest that the famous faces among us, meaning {NICKNAME} and Kinich — oh, and of course, Monsieur Neuvillette too — stay here for the time being.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: We'll empty the box, give it to Ororon, and then he can claim the item as if nothing happened.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: I'll follow to check if anyone is watching.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: I doubt anyone would recognize me anyway, so I shouldn't draw too much attention.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Keeping a low profile has its advantages.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: I think this plan is worth a try. I shall leave it to the pair of you.

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: So I have to go undercover again, right...?

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: Well, not exactly undercover. Just drop the Special Patrol persona and... be yourself instead.

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: Roger that. Over and out.

choices.text: Otherwise, we're gonna have to arrest you for real.
Let's just get down to business...
Please, anything but the Special Patrol!

talks.objective: Return to the entrance of the Palais Mermonia and carry out the plan

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: So, now that our crew's back together again, what's our next move?

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Oh! How about a game of rock paper scissors?

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: No chance! If I lose, we'll end up stuck in the room watching films all over again...

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Nope. This time, we'll only watch a film if I lose instead.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Had enough too, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Cacucu
dialogues.text: For real, now? C'mon, bro...

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Can we just ditch this whole "leaving it all to chance" thing? Why don't we take our fate into our own hands?

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Uhh... Aren't we doing that already? Rock paper scissors uses our hands...

dialogues.speaker: Cacucu
dialogues.text: Hahahaha!

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: ...Dunno why you're laughing, you're stuck with paper every time!

talks.objective: Head to the plaza as planned

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: (Nothing suspicious going on here either...)

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: (Strange... Maybe we're overthinking this?)

dialogues.speaker: Cacucu
dialogues.text: Oh dear! Oh dear!

dialogues.speaker: Argenteau
dialogues.text: Stop with the pecking... Stop with the pecking!

dialogues.speaker: Argenteau
dialogues.text: Please, sir, I'm begging you! Do me a favor and... get this pet of yours under control!

dialogues.speaker: Cacucu
dialogues.text: The heck are you on about?

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Sorry, but he's not my pet — he's my coworker.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: And I should warn you, he's not too happy with how you're talking about him...

dialogues.speaker: Argenteau
dialogues.text: What the!? This thing has a JOB? So in Natlan, they just dish out jobs to any old thing?

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Uh-oh, Cacucu's not too big on being called a "thing" either... You're on your own now.

dialogues.speaker: Argenteau
dialogues.text: I'm sorry, I'm sorry! Please, Mr. Cacucu! Master Cacucu, Lord Cacucu! I meant no offense, I promise!

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Alright, Cacucu, that'll do for now. Let me ask him some questions first.

dialogues.speaker: Cacucu
dialogues.text: Sure thing, bro!

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: (Ororon actually looks pretty serious this time. Was he just pretending to be clueless earlier?)

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: (Interesting... Think I'll sit back and see how this plays out.)

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: You actually got it? Wow, didn't think it would be that easy...

dialogues.speaker: Argenteau
dialogues.text: Ah, excellent! Looks like sending you was the right approach after all!

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: "After all"?

dialogues.speaker: Argenteau
dialogues.text: Uh... I mean, because the staff at the Palais Mermonia don't recognize you, right... Haha...

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: So I got it, but I don't remember promising I'd hand it over.

dialogues.speaker: Argenteau
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: This thing's pretty cool. I've taken a bit of a liking to it.

dialogues.speaker: Argenteau
dialogues.text: Please don't do this, my good sir, my master, my lord! My very life hangs in the balance...

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: (His life hangs in the balance...?)

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: If this means so much to you... what are you gonna offer me in return?

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: ...Are you trying to get him to say "my life"?

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Uhh... How'd you know that?

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Because I watched that film with you!

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: You should drop the act. We don't want a real misunderstanding on our hands.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: ...You're probably right. But honestly, I don't know what else to say.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Sorry, this is the most "myself" I can be. Is that enough?

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Enough. More than enough.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Uh, who's this dude...?

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Just think of me as a staff member from the Palais Mermonia.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Now, if you don't mind, I have some questions for this gentleman about that "life-or-death" treasure you were just discussing... Truthful answers appreciated, of course.

dialogues.speaker: Argenteau
dialogues.text: Oh no, I'm toast now...

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: What's that supposed to mean? You don't think the Palais Mermonia has the ability to protect our citizens?

dialogues.speaker: Argenteau
dialogues.text: No, no! I mean, yes, of course they do! I, uh... P—Please, ask away...

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: I could do that. But I'd rather you just tell the whole story, from the beginning.

dialogues.speaker: Argenteau
dialogues.text: *sigh*... I suppose I only have myself to blame. Such a rare antique, I couldn't resist...

dialogues.speaker: Argenteau
dialogues.text: I'm a collector of antiques — nothing excites me more than rare old relics. And to be completely honest... if someone's selling, I'm buying. I don't care to ask where they sourced their goods...

dialogues.speaker: Argenteau
dialogues.text: As for the seller of this particular item... Well, I've never met him in person.

dialogues.speaker: Argenteau
dialogues.text: We've had some prior dealings, but always under the cover of coded ads in some shady tabloids — lost-and-found notices, missing person ads, that sort of thing.

dialogues.speaker: Argenteau
dialogues.text: As long as I took care to hide a time and place somewhere within the text, then slipped some Mora into the envelope before submitting the ad, it would get published. And that was that — no fuss, no trace. Simple, right?

dialogues.speaker: Argenteau
dialogues.text: Normally, everything goes off without a hitch. But this time, I arrive at the pickup spot expecting a discreet in and out, and instead, I find a whole construction crew at work!

dialogues.speaker: Argenteau
dialogues.text: That was not what we'd agreed! But I couldn't just let it go, so I reached out to him again, the same way as usual.

dialogues.speaker: Argenteau
dialogues.text: He replied, and do you know what he said? He told me that the item's now in the Palais Mermonia!

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Well, he wasn't lying about that.

dialogues.speaker: Argenteau
dialogues.text: He insisted that it would be "inconvenient" for him to make an appearance himself, but said that if I could somehow find a way to retrieve it from the Palais, he'd give me a discount on the price...

dialogues.speaker: Argenteau
dialogues.text: Of course, it wasn't the discount that swung it! Do I look like I'm strapped for cash?

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Feeling smug now, are we?

dialogues.speaker: Cacucu
dialogues.text: Feeling smug now, are we?

dialogues.speaker: Argenteau
dialogues.text: No, no... Please, go easy on me!

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Go on.

dialogues.speaker: Argenteau
dialogues.text: Ah, where was I... Well anyway, I thought to myself, seeing as the item itself came from Natlan, it would make more sense if I could find someone from there to go retrieve it.

dialogues.speaker: Argenteau
dialogues.text: And by a stroke of complete and utter coincidence, I just so happened to see these two young folks wandering around, so I...

dialogues.speaker: Argenteau
dialogues.text: *sigh* I'm so very sorry, I underestimated the pair of you!

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: I need you to clear something up for me. You haven't paid the seller yet, correct? And yet, he told you to collect the item from the Palais Mermonia. Was he not worried that you'd just split afterwards?

dialogues.speaker: Argenteau
dialogues.text: Well... To be honest, though I can't claim to know him very well, he on the other hand seems to know my name and where I live...

dialogues.speaker: Argenteau
dialogues.text: Besides, this is a guy who managed to get his hands on an ancient Natlanese weapon. That's probably not the kind of person I want to double-cross...

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Fair. That makes sense.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: So, Mr...

dialogues.speaker: Argenteau
dialogues.text: Uh... Please, uh, just call me Argenteau.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Alright, Mr. Argenteau, listen very carefully to what I'm about to say. It will determine how much of the rest of your life you'll be spending beneath the waves.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: What does he mean? Is he gonna drown him, just like they do in those gangster films?

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: ...Oh, I get it! He's talking about that place at the bottom of the Fontainian sea...

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Shh, can it!

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Owing to your suspected involvement in the illicit trade of Natlanese relics, you're now one of the suspects in an international smuggling case.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: A trip to the Opera Epiclese seems unavoidable at this stage, but on the bright side, you still have one chance to make things right.

dialogues.speaker: Argenteau
dialogues.text: Okay... D—Do I really? Please, tell me what to do.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: It's very simple. Just reach out to your seller in the same way as usual, arrange to meet, bring the money, and make the deal. Just be sure to let me know all the details — I'm talking time, place, the whole lot.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: If we can catch the other party by doing this, you'll have gone some way toward redeeming yourself. Understand?

dialogues.speaker: Argenteau
dialogues.text: Oh... I see! I—I understand! You shall have my full and unadulterated cooperation!

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Good. Don't break the law, and don't even think about making a run for it. The Palais Mermonia will be watching you and ensuring your safety.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Alright, take the box, but leave your ID and other documents behind. You can go now.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: As for you two...

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: *sigh* Protocol dictates that I should take you both back to the Palais and have you sign a confidentiality agreement... But that would take a lot of time and effort.

dialogues.speaker: Cacucu
dialogues.text: Such a hassle, bro!

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: See, Mr. Cacucu knows exactly where I'm coming from.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: #So I was thinking, since you're all friends of {NICKNAME}...

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: I understand, Sir. We got dragged into this by accident, and it has diddly-squat to do with us.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: #Out of respect for {NICKNAME}, we won't say another word.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Ohhh, I know this part — we'd better keep our mouths shut, or we'll both be sleeping with the fishes in a tailor-made pair o' cement shoes.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: In that case, I understand completely.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: ...Not exactly what I was going for, but if that's how you want to understand it, then be my guest.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Mm, then it's settled. Thanks for your help.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: (Boy, am I glad that's over. That's enough work for one day... Time to head back!)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, Wriothesley's back!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Judging by your expression, it must be good news, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: It went smoothly, on the whole.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Wriothesley recounts what happened.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: It all makes perfect sense, but somehow it feels like Wriothesley has glossed over a lot of the "bro" talk...

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: ...So anyway, that was when I went and told the Fontainian guards about my suspicions.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: After an investigation and a chase, they finally apprehended them and sent them on their way.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, guess they're headed exactly where they should be!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Good job, Kinich!

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Thanks.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Based on your recollections just now...

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: *sigh* I was completely focused on those smugglers at the time, so I wasn't really paying attention to other passersby.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That's only natural. Don't worry about it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, Kinich, you did great!

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: In other words, the person who brought the gun here — the one who "lost" it — has no connection to the smugglers whatsoever. They were working entirely on their own.

dialogues.speaker: Cacucu
dialogues.text: Oh dear! Oh dear!

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Sounds like Mr. Cacucu wants to chime in?

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: He said this elusive individual's actions are positively mystifying.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: It's a good observation. I quite agree.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: However, we still know next to nothing about the person. Perhaps we should start by focusing on the "lost" item itself.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: It certainly seems like it was the bait in some kind of trap.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: The only question is, why wasn't the bait made more conspicuous?

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Hmm...

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Has something... sprung to mind?

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: I just remembered a film I watched this one time.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Cacucu
dialogues.text: Oh wow... No way, bro!

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Hold on, let me explain...

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: #Just now, {NICKNAME} speculated that this box might have been placed there on purpose, as if the intention was for someone to come pick it up. That got me thinking about those films about kidnapping cases.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: When they demand their ransom, the kidnappers tell the victim's family to leave money or valuables at a designated spot for someone to come pick up.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: That doesn't merely happen in films. There have been similar cases in real life.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: In fact, if anything, it's probably the real-life events that inspired the films.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Mm, sounds plausible.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, wait, wait, wait, wait... This raises the stakes to a whole new level...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If the gun really was some kind of ransom, then... since we took the box, the kidnappers never got their payment, so...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: D—Does that mean they... executed the hostage?

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: I agree. I don't believe we have a kidnapping on our hands.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: Selling off stolen goods is extra work that most kidnappers would want to avoid. Unless they're after something very specific, they tend to just ask for cash.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: Could we be dealing with a kidnapper who's dead set on getting their hands on an ancient dragon handgun? It's not impossible, but the likelihood is very slim. We can discount that possibility for now.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: And speaking of selling stolen goods... Don't you think this looks more like a transaction?

choices.text: We haven't heard of any missing people.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's been a few days. The ban on flying objects should be over by now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's head over to the Palais Mermonia to see how Cacucu's doing!

dialogues.speaker: Chajal
dialogues.text: Hehe, nice thinking, boss. This tourist tub's been fast-going and smooth-sailing, plus no one's been asking us what we're up to.

dialogues.speaker: Banolkax
dialogues.text: Hehe, that goes without saying. A big cargo ship would have been too slow, whereas the smaller ones would have been faster but way too bumpy.

dialogues.speaker: Banolkax
dialogues.text: If we ended up damaging the goods by accident, all these months spent grafting away would have gone up in smoke.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: (Seriously? But there's hardly anything here... Would it really have taken them months to prepare? And why would they need to transport it with such care?)

dialogues.speaker: Chajal
dialogues.text: Who goes there?

dialogues.speaker: Banolkax
dialogues.text: What was that sound?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (This is a relic left behind by Natlan's ancient dragon civilization. It's a genuine antique, so it must be of great value.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (A genuine treasure lost by the roadside, yet still it remains unreported and unclaimed...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (It doesn't seem like an accident. No, it's as if someone left it there on purpose...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Why would someone just leave such a valuable antique out in the middle of nowhere... Was the plan for someone to come pick it up?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (That doesn't sound right... I need to think about this some more.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (The gun was placed in a locked box and hidden away. Clearly, the seller wanted to keep their identity a secret.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (After receiving the instructions, the buyer would have gone to the designated spot with the money to pick up the goods. To ensure they actually got paid, the seller would likely have been watching the buyer.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Before the buyer could show up, Lepine-Pauline found the goods by chance while setting up the event venue.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Due to the unexpected arrival of Film Fantasyland, the deal had to be called off.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (That doesn't sound right... I need to think about this some more.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The lost-and-found notice is up!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Maybe we should go hang around the Palais Mermonia to see if anyone shows up to claim it?

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: (No sign of any suspicious individuals around here...)

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: (Ororon has entered the elevator as planned. I'll head over to the plaza now.)

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: (Ororon's taking the elevator. I should take a different route to the plaza.)

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: (This isn't the way that Ororon said. Am I getting too old to remember directions...?)

dialogues.speaker: Kanaka
dialogues.text: Who goes there?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You need to be more careful. Stay hidden, make use of distractions, and don't get caught this time...

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: (Could they be secretly smuggling precious items out of Natlan...? I'll need to find a way to get to the bottom of this.)
